title: How Enterprise AI Really Gets Deployed

reader_summary.headline: Enterprises deploy AI using small models for tasks and big models for experiments.
reader_summary.overview: Companies use small, open-source models for specific tasks because they are faster and cheaper. Big models remain necessary for new experiments or complex jobs like finding trends in millions of conversations. Enterprises will eventually switch to open-source models, but security rules and the need for dedicated teams to train new versions mean the transition takes time.

key_points.text: Companies use small, open-source models for specific tasks because they are faster and cheaper than big models.
key_points.evidence_quote: today, 90% of a workflow is on open source. On the specific task we want them to do, they actually outperform the large, smart, state-of-the-art model.

key_points.text: Big models are still needed for new experiments or complex jobs like reviewing millions of conversations to find trends.
key_points.evidence_quote: for everything that's new and sort of experimental, or you're, let us just say what, or like kind of these products where you really need the intelligence, you're still going to use Frontier models.

key_points.text: Using small models is not a trade-off; they can be tuned to match the performance of big models on specific tasks.
key_points.evidence_quote: even if you have a quote, dumb or model, you can get it, and we've seen this in practice, you can get it to higher performance on that specific task.

key_points.text: Companies need a dedicated team to constantly train new versions of open-source models as technology improves.
key_points.evidence_quote: We've really built it to compress the time between new model coming out, and useful fine-tuned to our task model popping out the other end, just because it happens all the time.

key_points.text: Application layer software will stay because humans need tools to store data and organize work, even with advanced AI.
key_points.evidence_quote: I don't think software is whole in any meaningful ways going away. And I still think, you know, on the application layer, there's so many different kinds of work that need to be done that can be done faster, more efficiently, more cheaply.

positions.commentary: The speaker concludes that their view on the future of CRMs is bullish.

thesis: The episode argues that CRMs will remain valuable in the future of Enterprise AI because they hold the source of truth for data that AI agents need to access. The speaker explicitly states that CRMs could do quite well as agents utilize them, concluding with a bullish view on their future prospects.

claims.claim: The speaker believes CRMs will remain valuable as they hold the source of truth for data that AI agents need to access.
claims.quote: And I think when we have these AI agents, they will need somewhere to put that information.
